title: Prove the sharp integer job-splitting charge (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Proves the least universal coefficient for the exact integer split `R=qJ+r>J`, `0<=r<J`, at every real `0<t<1`:

```text
q J^t + r^t <= K_t R J^(t-1)
K_t = (1+s_t^t)/(1+s_t) = t s_t^(t-1)
t s_t^(t-1) - (1-t)s_t^t = 1,  0<s_t<1

higher-moment sufficient charge:
alpha^v + 2 gamma_u^v + 2 delta^v
             becomes
alpha^v + K_t gamma_u^v + 2 delta^v
```

The coefficient is optimal over integer jobs and satisfies `1<K_t<2`. At `t=1/2` it is `(1+sqrt(2))/2`; at `t=1/3` it is `4/3`, attained by `J=8,R=9`.

Claim type: scoped analytic proof with exact finite corroboration. Only `research/sharp-integer-split-charge/` is added. This tightens one estimate of zxv's #4433 while retaining the tensor, native and completion premises. It does not assert a new kappa or a smaller tensor power. The calculus is elementary; no literature-priority claim is made. The merged #4483 direct compiler removes these steps for certain profiles under its own gates; this does not improve its sufficient ranks.

Produced by Nick Petalas. Credit zxv/#4433, Cinna Davis/#4412/#4414/#4416 and Jacob Alan Sussman for the retained strictification, chronological product and integer compiler, with their existing predecessor attribution. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Apache-2.0.

## Evidence

- Before: the retained split-tail estimate uses coefficient 2. After: the written maximization and integer approximation prove the optimal `K_t`; no predecessor executable is used as the deliverable.
- Both registered warning-strict normal and optimized checks pass all 56,448 enumerated split cases, seven integer sharpness sequences, the half/third-exponent closed forms and eleven rejection controls. Rational polynomial and integer-root enclosures use no floating-point acceptance.
- Locally timed registered commands took 0.25 and 0.26 seconds on CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64. Package metadata/replay, diff checks and six-file committed-byte/source-history preflight pass at `3f60fe0c90573a60e52d016b0001f4d24f6db2ae`.
- A committed-byte export passes optimized isolated replay with no Git and `PATH=/nonexistent`; all six source/export files remain unchanged. Separate altered-source and altered-receipt copies reject with `receipt or source-hash mismatch`.

Distinctive all-main README and merged-PR searches were checked separately.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The all-real-exponent statement is a written analytic proof. Finite checks cover six exponents on `J<=48,q<=8` plus seven sharpness sequences through `J=10^6`; they are not a formal proof. Native correctness/admission, a new supplier inventory, a reduced tensor power, physical hosting/precision, the selected cold replay and the complete multiplication theorem were not checked or claimed. The sharp constant here is for the linear-rank comparison; the subsequent higher-moment transfer need not be sharp.

## Open next questions

- Apply the coefficient to one pinned, fully charged inventory to decide whether it reduces a sufficient tensor power; preserve the certified moment intervals, completion and outer bill.
- Determine the least direct coefficient for fixed `sigma>1` in `split_t(R,J)<=K_(t,sigma) R^sigma J^(t-sigma)`, starting with one normalized quotient.

## Related open work

No open PR found in the inspected live bodies targets this sharp integer split coefficient. #4814 studies ordinary BIT finite leaf backends, a separate supplier/leaf comparison; this contribution computes none of its saving numbers and does not assess its admission claims.

This account's open PRs created since the CLAIM at 2026-10-22 21:13:18 UTC were refreshed before DONE. The nine other new open submissions concern different objects or quantities; none computes this split coefficient or the same oversized-paid tail term. No additional same-object related-work entry or numerical disagreement was found.
